● Summary

  - Herdr Slack plugin bridges Slack bot DMs to local Herdr sessions on Windows, enabling remote agent control and notifications via a per-user Slack app using Socket Mode.
  - Slash commands (/herdr list, /herdr new, /herdr send, /herdr status) support listing agents, starting new agents with modal config, sending prompts to live agents, and checking
    bridge status.
  - Modal-driven UI uses Block Kit dropdowns for workspace/agent selection and multiline input for prompts; also supports direct command execution with arguments.
  - Thread-based notifications maintain one DM thread per agent session with status updates (working/done/blocked), completion results, and mute controls; PC-originated agents
    notify only on working→done transitions.
  - Dedicated bridge workspace (herdr-slack) runs the plugin in isolation with Socket Mode event subscriptions, state persistence in .env, and owner-only access control.

  herdr tab create --workspace <ws> --label <label> --cwd <cwd> --no-focus

● I'll check the git configuration to understand the project context.

  Based on the specification document, here's a comprehensive breakdown of the herdr-slackbot design:

  ---

  1. Plugin Architecture & Core Purpose

  - The herdr-slackbot is a Herdr plugin (version 0.8.2+) for Windows that bridges Slack bot direct messages to the local Herdr session
  - Built with Python 3.11 using the slack_bolt framework in Socket Mode for real-time event handling
  - Restricted to owner-only access: one Slack app per user/PC to ensure isolation and security
  - The plugin enables remote agent management and status notifications directly from Slack DMs
  - Designed for standalone local installation via herdr plugin link or GitHub distribution via herdr plugin install

  2. Command Interface & User Interactions

  - The slash command name is configurable via .env SLASH_COMMAND variable, defaulting to /herdr-<windows username> (lowercased and sanitized)
  - /herdr <cmd> supports four primary commands: list (show agents), new (start agent), send (prompt agent), status (bridge health)
  - Commands without arguments trigger a Block Kit modal with interactive dropdowns and multiline text input; with arguments execute directly
  - Bot display name defaults to Herdr (<username>) but is configurable via BOT_DISPLAY_NAME environment variable
  - Unknown commands or bare /herdr invocation displays usage information

  3. Agent Spawning & Workspace Management

  - New agents spawn as tabs in selected Herdr workspaces using herdr tab create --workspace <ws> --label <label> --cwd <cwd> --no-focus
  - Modal fields for agent creation include: workspace selection, working directory (prefilled from existing panes, editable), agent kind (claude or codex), model, effort level,
    permission mode, optional name, and prompt text
  - Claude agents default to --model opus --effort high --permission-mode auto with effort options low|medium|high|xhigh|max
  - Agent names follow pattern [a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31} or auto-generate as slack-<N> with monotonic counter persistence
  - Unnamed agents receive auto-generated tab labels combining the auto-name with a prompt summary

  4. Agent Communication & Message Flow

  - Messages are sent to agent panes only (not shell panes or generic pane runners) using herdr agent send <name> <text> after acknowledging Slack first
  - Target selection dropdown displays comprehensive labels: <status emoji> · <name or pane_id> · <workspace label> · <status> · <terminal title>, truncated to Slack's 75-character
    limit
  - Only idle and done agent states accept new prompts; working state triggers a "busy" DM response
  - blocked state or Herdr agent_blocked errors trigger "needs confirmation on PC" notifications
  - Unknown agent states are rejected with error feedback to the user

  ┌────────────────┬─────────────────────────┬──────────┐
  │    Feature     │          Scope          │  Status  │
  ├────────────────┼─────────────────────────┼──────────┤
  │ Agent Commands │ List, New, Send, Status │ D1/D2/D5 │
  ├────────────────┼─────────────────────────┼──────────┤
  │ Threading      │ Per agent session       │ D7-D11   │
  ├────────────────┼─────────────────────────┼──────────┤
  │ Result Parsing │ Claude + Codex fallback │ D10      │
  └────────────────┴─────────────────────────┴──────────┘

  5. Thread Organization & Notifications

  - Each agent maintains exactly one DM thread bound to its agent_session id (not pane), created on first notification
  - Slack-sent confirmation message serves as thread root; replies include "⏳ started (working)" status update and final result upon completion
  - Agent state changes trigger immediate DM replies without timeout; completion detection uses event subscriptions
  - Mute controls ([🔕 mute] button) per agent thread allow selective notification suppression, persisted in state
  - PC-originated agents notify only on working → done transitions (skipping working → idle), while Slack-originated tasks always receive completion replies

  6. Result Display & Content Handling

  - Agent output is retrieved via herdr agent read <target> --source recent-unwrapped --lines 200, with trailing blank lines stripped
  - Claude results are parsed by identifying the echoed prompt line, extracting content between the prompt echo and the completion marker (✻), and capturing the last ● block
  - Fallback parsing (codex or parse failures) uses raw last N non-blank lines (e.g., 40 lines)
  - Content exceeding 3000 characters is truncated with a [전체 보기] (View Full) button that uploads the complete result as a markdown file
  - Result headers display: ✅ <name> · <workspace label> · <duration> plus context (cwd, terminal title); blocked states show ⚠️ prefix with "needs confirmation" note

  7. Bridge Runtime & Infrastructure

  - The bridge process runs in a dedicated Herdr workspace named herdr-slack, created automatically by plugin startup hooks if absent
  - Single-instance enforcement via lock file in STATE_DIR prevents duplicate bridge instances
  - Configuration stored in .env under HERDR_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR (obtained via herdr plugin config-dir <id>)
  - Herdr plugin actions and key bindings (if supported) enable restart and status commands accessible from the desktop
  - Logging writes to STATE_DIR log file and stdout with no sensitive credentials exposed

  8. Security, Setup & Distribution

  - Per-user Slack app configuration uses a manifest (YAML/JSON) generated with the user's slash command name, bot display name, Socket Mode enabled, and required scopes
    (chat:write, commands, im:history, im:write, files:write, users:read)
  - Bridge validates all incoming commands, actions, views, and messages against SLACK_OWNER_USER_ID; non-owner requests are ignored or rejected
  - User creates the Slack app from manifest and provides SLACK_BOT_TOKEN (xoxb) and SLACK_APP_TOKEN (xapp) in .env
  - Slack transport is isolated behind an interface for future extension to relay hubs
  - Project structure follows: herdr_slackbot/ package with modules for config, Herdr client, events, state, parsing, Slack app, blocks, and orchestration

  # Example: Starting a new agent
  herdr agent start slack-42 --kind claude --pane <root_pane_id> -- --model opus --effort high --permission-mode auto
  herdr agent prompt slack-42 "Analyze the repository structure"
